edits:
The October 4 continuation files the completed entry/maintenance project without confusing its original Keycloak checks with later real local Auth0 completion or still-open hosted/two-account acceptance. [PD04](maintainers/production-deployment.md) now explicitly requires a release gate covering creator edits and already-admitted continuations: ordinary maintenance deliberately leaves creator editing available and cannot alone establish a frozen replacement boundary. [EWF04](maintainers/extensible-world-foundation.md#ewf04--generic-permitted-inspection-context-and-presentation) records the current English-status-driven lighting defect, with bundled light/sky extraction retained by BW06 and renderer quality retained by SW18. The shadow and three-times-scene plans distinguish the delivered mercenary and later storage/cognition improvements from unqualified combined workloads, and historical save-reset permission is not reused. These are source-backed documentation corrections, not new runtime fixes or qualification.
Mike authorized [E08 entry and MP03 maintenance](projects/completed/multiplayer-entry-maintenance.md). A grant may now omit a character: characterless operator/spectator sessions never play, hold no control lease, stay out of exit and shared-pause accounting, and reach only an explicit route allowlist. A new `spectate` capability shows a generic public overview without names, identities, possessions or speech. Access managers issue hashed, single-use, expiring, revocable invites redeemed through the existing OIDC sign-in; a player invite binds an unowned person in the same world commit as its grant. This supersedes the “operator provisioning only” and “play plus character for every session” limits ([MP02/MP05](limits/multiplayer.md#mp02)); open public sign-up stays out of scope as [D68](../archive/05-project/open-decisions.md#d68--world-entry-beyond-invites). Characterless grants reuse the existing grant row with an internal marker. The original rationale incorrectly treated the development-save policy as a prohibition on changing that column; it forbids legacy support, not coherent current-model schema changes. The marker remains the implemented representation, not a compatibility requirement. The completed project links the controlling policy and preserves current account/control integrity.
files.summary: record release and lighting findings and correct schema-policy rationale
